tools.name: Newcastle Ottawa Scale–Education (NOS-E)
tools.description:
This tool is modified from the original NOS scale to adapt to a broader range of study types in educational literature, such as nonrandomized and observational studies. The changes include: removing 3 items (ascertainment of

candidates.name: QAISER
candidates.study: Systematic literature reviews in software engineering
candidates.fit: Assesses the methodological quality of completed reviews. It adapts AMSTAR 2 to software engineering and contains 15 items.
candidates.evidence: Four external experts reviewed the instrument; the authors demonstrated it on six reviews. This supports content and usability, but does not establish broad independent reliability.
candidates.vet: Prioritize for the software engineering gap. Check whether assessment of secondary studies fits the repository scope.

candidates.name: ROBFEAD
candidates.study: Finite element analysis studies in dentistry
candidates.fit: Six domains and 22 guiding questions assess risk of bias in dental finite element research. This directly addresses simulation research in a narrow engineering setting.
candidates.evidence: The development paper describes a validation phase. Its abstract does not establish a general interrater or intrarater coefficient; the full validation methods should be checked.
candidates.vet: Prioritize for engineering. Any use in general finite element physics would be an adaptation requiring evaluation.

candidates.name: ToxRTool
candidates.study: In vivo and in vitro toxicological studies
candidates.fit: Evaluates the inherent quality of toxicological data using explicit criteria and reliability categories. In this context, data reliability means study quality, not interrater reliability of the instrument.
candidates.evidence: Development paper and a 2015 external evaluation are available. Read both before making a general validation claim.
candidates.vet: Review the study-quality criteria. Do not treat its category score as interchangeable with domain-specific risk of bias.

candidates.name: SciRAP for in vivo toxicity studies
candidates.fit: Evaluates methodological and reporting quality separately from relevance. The quality component is potentially in scope; the relevance component needs a separate decision.
candidates.evidence: Expert testing and refinement reported in 2018. A later systematic-review comparison explicitly states that it is not a validation of SciRAP in that context.
candidates.vet: Include only if Leila accepts the methodological quality component. Keep relevance judgments separate.

candidates.name: CRED including the sediment and soil extension
candidates.study: Aquatic, sediment and soil ecotoxicity studies
candidates.fit: The evaluation method has explicit study-quality criteria and separate relevance criteria. It also has reporting recommendations, which should not be mistaken for the assessment tool.
candidates.evidence: A ring test compared CRED with Klimisch. A 2024 extension adds soil and sediment considerations. Transfer of the original evaluation results to the extension is not established here.
candidates.vet: Potential fit for pesticide and soil ecotoxicity evidence. This is not a universal agricultural field-trial tool.

candidates.name: RoBiNT
candidates.study: Single-case experimental designs and n-of-1 trials
candidates.fit: Contains separate internal-validity and external-validity/interpretation subscales. The internal-validity component directly addresses methodological bias.
candidates.evidence: 2013 evaluation supports discriminative validity and excellent interrater reliability. Reported total-score ICC was 0.90 for experienced raters and 0.88 for trained novices in the evaluated sample.
candidates.vet: Prioritize for single-case psychology research. Decide whether to record the full instrument or distinguish its subscales.

candidates.name: Cambridge Quality Checklists
candidates.study: Studies of correlates, risk factors and causal risk factors for offending
candidates.fit: Assesses methodological quality of empirical criminological studies. It is a study-appraisal instrument, not a tool for judging legal arguments or case law.
candidates.evidence: 2012 study evaluated 60 studies of disrupted families and offending, reporting high interrater reliability and generally larger effects in lower-quality studies. Authors recommend refinement.
candidates.vet: Suitable candidate for the empirical law and criminal-justice gap. Do not generalize to doctrinal legal scholarship.

candidates.name: QUADAS-3
candidates.fields: Diagnostic research; selected medical physics applications
candidates.fit: Updated diagnostic accuracy risk-of-bias instrument. Adds an ideal test accuracy trial concept, estimate-level assessment and an analysis domain.
candidates.evidence: Development publication exists. This review has not established independent psychometric validation of the new version. QUADAS-2 estimates must not be transferred automatically.
candidates.vet: Consider an update alongside the existing QUADAS-2 entry. Medical physics use is an inferred design-based fit, not evidence of validation across physics.

candidates.name: PROBAST+AI
candidates.study: Clinical prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence
candidates.fit: Updates quality, risk-of-bias and applicability assessment for prediction model development and evaluation. It does not validate arbitrary machine learning benchmarks.
candidates.evidence: 2025 development paper is available. Independent reliability evidence for this exact revision was not established in this review.
candidates.vet: Prioritize for the clinical AI subset. Preserve the distinction between general computer science and health prediction models.

candidates.name: JBI textual evidence checklists
candidates.study: Narrative evidence, expert opinion and policy text
candidates.fit: JBI now provides three separate checklists in place of the older general text/opinion approach. They assess authenticity, credibility and argument structure.
candidates.evidence: 2025 methodology paper explains development and appraisal. An independent reliability evaluation was not located.
candidates.vet: Review each checklist for scope before adding it. Policy-text credibility is not necessarily methodological quality or risk of bias in an empirical study. Compare with text/opinion and NOTARI rows.

candidates.name: ROBINS-I V2
candidates.study: Nonrandomized follow-up studies of intervention effects
candidates.fit: Adds algorithms for suggested judgments and revises bias assessment. The current developer page explicitly labels the November 2025 version a draft.
candidates.evidence: Developer guidance is available. Reliability findings for the 2016 instrument do not establish performance of V2.
candidates.vet: Track as a draft and record the exact date. Do not silently replace the established ROBINS-I entry.

candidates.name: CEE Critical Appraisal Tool formal version
candidates.study: Comparative quantitative environmental studies of causal effects
candidates.fit: Directly evaluates risk of bias using criteria that feed an overall judgment. Its environmental scope can cover relevant agronomy questions after design-specific assessment.
candidates.evidence: Formal version published 11 October 2026 after prototype use, user feedback and revision. The paper calls for further evaluation; a general reliability claim is premature.
candidates.vet: Update the existing version 0.3 record after comparing items and confirming the version. This is not a wholly new tool family.

candidates.name: SciRAPepi
candidates.study: Cross-sectional, case-control, nested case-control and cohort studies of chemical exposure
candidates.fit: Evaluates study reliability and relevance for chemical hazard and risk assessment. Keep methodological evaluation separate from relevance to a policy question.
candidates.evidence: 2026 development paper reports expert testing by 37 epidemiologists and risk assessors on four studies, followed by refinement. Wider independent validation remains open.
candidates.vet: Consider as a separate study-design instrument within the SciRAP family. Confirm which components meet the repository scope.
